SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r1.claim: ‘I will come’ conveys resolve while ‘perhaps I will come’ conveys hope; ordinary speech can move from certainty to qualification as circumstances intervene, so the paired expressions are not contradictory.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r1.anchor: يقول أحدنا سآتي اليوم لعلي أستطيع بمعنى (أقطع ثم أترجّى)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r2.claim: The certainty of al-Naml fits its atmosphere of strength and empowerment; al-Qasas is shaped by fear from before Moses’ birth, fitting the hopeful wording.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r2.anchor: المقام كله في سورة النمل مبني على القطع والقوة والتمكين أما سورة القصص فهي مبنيّة على الخوف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r3.claim: A flaming shihab gives more warmth and light, whereas a jadhwa need not contain flame; the less assured ember suits al-Qasas’ fearful setting.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r3.anchor: الشهاب هو شعلة من النار والشهاب أنفع في الدفء والإستنارة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r1.claim: He gives jadhwa as an ember or firebrand; other explanations call it wood remaining after burning or a stick with fire but no flame.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r1.anchor: فهي الجمرة أو القبسة من النار وقيل: هي ما يبقى من الحطب بعد الالتهاب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r2.claim: The shihab is better than the ember for warmth and illumination because it bears a bright flame.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r2.anchor: الشهاب يدفىء أكثر من الجمرة لما فيه من اللهب الساطع، كما أنه ينفع في الاستنارة أيضاً.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r3.claim: Saying he will fetch a shihab kindled from the fire signals resolve and courage; the less certain jadhwa suits fear, while the shihab fits a scene without fear.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r3.anchor: وهذا أدلّ على القوة وثبات الجنان، لأن معناه أنه سيذهب إلى النار ويقبس منها شعلة ساطعة.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r1.claim: The repeated coming in al-Naml signals Moses’ confidence and strength; he does not repeat the verb in al-Qasas, fitting its fearful atmosphere.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r1.anchor: فأكد الإتيان في سورة النمل لقوة يقينه وثقته بنفسه، والتوكيد يدل على القوة، في حين لم يكرر فعل الإتيان في القصص مناسبة لجو الخوف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r2.claim: The verb for coming appears twelve times in al-Naml and six in al-Qasas, so repeating ātiikum suits al-Naml throughout.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r2.anchor: إن فعل (الإتيان) تكرر في النمل اثنتي عشرة مرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r3.claim: He defines shihāb as a bright flame and qabas as flame taken from a larger fire, citing lexicons for these senses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r3.anchor: والشهاب: هو شعلة من النار ساطعة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r4.claim: Qabas can also be used of acquiring knowledge, as in the expression qabasa al-ʿilma, ‘he acquired knowledge.’
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r4.anchor: يقال: قبس يقبس منه نارا، أي: أخذ منه نارا، وقبس العلمَ استفاده

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r7.claim: The bright flame is better than an ember because its blazing flame gives more warmth and also provides light.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r7.anchor: والمجيء بالشهاب أحسن من المجيء بالجمرة، لأن الشهاب يدفئ أكثر من الجمرة لما فيه من اللهب الساطع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r8.claim: Calling it a flame taken from the fire rather than snatched or carried shows strength and resolve: Moses will go to the fire and take a bright flame.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r8.anchor: وهذا أدل على القوة وثبات الجنان، لأن معناه أنه سيذهب إلى النار، ويقبس منها شعلة نار ساطعة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r1.claim: Al-Naml uses the future sīn for emphasis and certainty, while al-Qasas uses laʿallī to express hope.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r1.anchor: في سورة النمل جاء بالسين في (سآتيكم) والسين تفيد التوكيد، أما في القصص فجاء بـ (لعلي آتيكم) وهي للترجّي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r2.claim: Speakers can commit and then hope circumstances allow it, or the reverse; the scene determines whether the wording conveys hope or certainty.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r2.anchor: يقول أحدنا سآتي اليوم لعلي أستطيع بمعنى (أقطع ثم أترجّى)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r3.claim: Al-Naml’s scene is built on certainty, strength, and empowerment; al-Qasas’ scene is built on fear reaching back to before Moses’ birth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r3.anchor: المقام كله في سورة النمل مبني على القطع والقوة والتمكين أما سورة القصص فهي مبنيّة على الخوف من قبل ولادة موسى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r4.claim: A bright, warming, illuminating flame fits al-Naml’s confident scene; a mere ember that may not contain fire fits al-Qasas’ fearful scene.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r4.anchor: الشهاب أنفع في الدفء والإستنارة، أما في القصص فقال تعالى (أو جذوة من النار) والجذوة ليس بالضرورة أن يكون فيها نار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r5.claim: Quranic speech accurately conveys events in a highly crafted style; each wording is correct and shaped for its context, like choosing tactful terms when speaking to an elder.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r5.anchor: القرآن هو ترجمة للأحداث والأقوال لكن مصوغ صياغة فنّية عالية

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p460/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p460/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p460/r7.claim: Moses was sent to Pharaoh with nine clear signs, yet Pharaoh and his people rejected him despite recognizing their divine origin and were destroyed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p460/r7.anchor: God sent him as a messenger to the Pharaoh with nine blatant signs.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r11.claim: The accusative idh may depend on an implied “remember,” or on “Knowing,” though the latter attachment is unclear because it would restrict the adjective with a complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r11.anchor: قيل: وانتصب إذ باذكر مضمرة، أو بعليم وليس انتصابه بعليم واضحا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r12.claim: The account in Ṭā Hā has already covered Moses's journey with his family; although “family” is plural, one report says only his wife accompanied him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r12.anchor: وقد تقدم طرف من قصة موسى عليه السلام في رحلته بأهله من مدين: في سورة طه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r13.claim: Another report says Moses's wife had borne him a son while he was with Shuʿayb, and the son was with his mother; if accurate, the plural is an honorific address.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r13.anchor: وقيل: كانت ولدت له، وهو عند شعيب، ولدا، فكان مع أمه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r14.claim: At night in cold weather, Moses had lost the route; seeing fire gave hope of directions or of a flame for warmth if nobody could guide him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r14.anchor: وكان الطريق قد اشتبه عليه، والوقت بارد، والسير في ليل، فتشوقت نفسه، إذ رأى النار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r15.claim: The alternatives with aw express either finding someone to guide the traveling party or, if they must stay, bringing fire to warm themselves, not both needs at once.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p209/r15.anchor: فليس محتاجا للشيئين معا، بل لأحدهما الخبر إن وجد من يخبره فيرحل، أو الاصطلاء إن لم يجد وأقام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r1.claim: The wording varies across the surahs: here Moses says he will bring news, Ṭā Hā says perhaps fire, and al-Qaṣaṣ says perhaps news; strong hope can be stated confidently despite possible failure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r1.anchor: وجاء هنا: سآتيكم منها بخبر، وهو خبر، وفي طه: لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r2.claim: The future prefix sīn may signal the distance to the fire or allow for a delay along the way.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r2.anchor: وأتى بسين الاستقبال، إما لأن المسافة كانت بعيدة، وإما لأنه قد يمكن أن يبطىء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r3.claim: A shihāb is a flame; a qabas is fire carried off, a passive-like noun for a piece of fire on a stick or similar object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r3.anchor: والشهاب: الشعلة، والقبس: النار المقبوسة، فعل بمعنى مفعول، وهو القطعة من النار في عود أو غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r4.speaker: قراءة الكوفيين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r4.claim: The Kūfan readers vocalize shihāb with nunation and read qabas as its apposition or an adjective, since it means kindled fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r4.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون: بشهاب منونا، فقبس بدل أو صفة، لأنه بمعنى المقبوس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r5.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r5.claim: The remaining seven readers, along with al-Ḥasan, read the two nouns in a genitive construct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r5.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة: بالإضافة، وهي قراءة الحسن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī, following Abū al-Ḥasan, explains the construct as distinguishing a flame that is a firebrand from one that is not; Abū al-Ḥasan says this reading is better and more common.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p210/r6.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أضاف الشهاب إلى القبس، لأنه يكون قبسا وغير قبس، واتبع في ذلك أبا الحسن.

STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.claim: The account then recounts Moses encountering fire on the mountain, where God charged him to go to Pharaoh and free the Israelites.
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r4.anchor: turns to Moses’ encounter with the fire on the mountain, from which God spoke charging him with his mission

SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r1.claim: Idh qāla may be governed by an omitted remember or know, inferred from ʿalīm or ḥalīm; al-Samīn finds this weak because it binds the attribute to this circumstance.
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون منصوبا بإضمار اذكر أو تعلم مقدرا

SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r2.claim: The Kufans use nunation on shihāb, parsing qabas either as an appositive or as an adjective meaning something taken as a firebrand.
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r2.anchor: قرأ الكوفيون بتنوين " شهاب " على أن قبسا بدل

SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r3.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r3.claim: The other readers use genitive annexation as an explanatory relation, since a shihāb may be a firebrand or something else.
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r3.anchor: والباقون بالإضافة على البيان؛ لأن الشهاب يكون قبسا وغيره

SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r4.claim: A shihāb is a flame, while a qabas is a piece of it, whether or not it is on a stick.

SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r5.claim: Aw has its ordinary sense of offering alternatives of different kinds.
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r5.anchor: على بابها من التنويع. والطاء في

SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r6.claim: The ṭāʾ in taṣṭalūn replaces the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form, from ṣaliya bi-l-nār.
SAMIN-DURR:27:7/r6.anchor: والطاء في " تصطلون " بدل من تاء الافتعال

ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n6/r1.claim: Asad points to the account in 20:9 onward, especially note 7 on 20:10.
ASAD-NOTES:27:7#n6/r1.anchor: Cf. 20:9 ff., and particularly note 7 on verse 10 of that surah.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p368/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p368/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p368/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses shihāb qabas as a flame from which they can take fire; Ṭarafa's verse supplies a poetic usage of qabas.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p368/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: شعلة من نار يقتبسون منها.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p368/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p368/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p368/r3.claim: The Qur'an uses shihāb in singular and plural, including verses about a pursued listener and guarded heavens.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p368/r3.anchor: وجاء شهاب، مفرداً وجمعاً، في آيات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r1.claim: Moses’ promise in al-Naml is firmer than his hope in al-Qaṣaṣ, and a blazing brand is harder to bring than an ember.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r1.anchor: فقط قطع في النمل على نفسه أن يأتيهم بخبرٍ أو شهابٍ قبس، في حين ترجّى ذلك في القصص. والقطع أشق وأصعب من الترجي

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r1.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r1.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read shihāban qabasan, with tanwīn and no annexation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r1.anchor: فقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي (بشهاب قبس) منونا غير مضاف

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r2.claim: The other readers annex qabas to shihāb without tanwīn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: (بشهاب قبس) مضاف غير منون

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses shihāb as fire and qabas as what has been kindled or taken from it; Abu Zubayd's شعلة القبس associates the term with a flame.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r3.anchor: أبو عبيدة: (بشهاب قبس): الشهاب: النار، والقبس ما اقتبست

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r4.claim: Another explanation calls any bright, luminous object a shihāb; the author is unsure whether this was transmitted or inferred, and a poem illustrates fire as thāqib, piercing or bright.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r4.anchor: غيره: كل أبيض ذي نور فهو شهاب، ولا أدري أقاله رواية أم استدلالا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r5.claim: Qabas can be an adjective meaning something kindled, derived from qabastuhu; if adjectival it should follow shihāb, but if a verbal noun it can be annexed to it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون القبس صفة، ويجوز أن يكون اسما غير صفة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r6.claim: The author compares qabas with ḥalab, which can mean the act of milking or the milk obtained, and cites the verbal-noun pattern بدا له يبدو بدأ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r6.anchor: حلب يحلب حلبا، فيجوز في قولهم: حلبا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r7.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r7.claim: The cited line attributed to al-Afwah calls a gleaming thrown spear a shihāb, while Aws compares a falling meteor's trail and rising flame; both support luminous projectile imagery.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r7.anchor: فأما قول الشاعر يروى للأفوه : كشهاب القذف يرميكم به

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r8.claim: If qabas is adjectival, it should agree with its head, as maq būs describes ḍarm in the cited comparison; an adjective does not form an annexation with its noun.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r8.anchor: فالأحسن أن يجري على الشهاب كما جرى على الموصوف في قوله

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r9.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r9.claim: The line قابس أهله لم يقبس illustrates the active participle for someone who brings or takes fire; al-Tirmah's comparison provides a related image of seeking water in a barren place.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p372/r9.anchor: قال الشاعر: في حيث خالطت الخزامى عرفجا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r1.claim: The construct reading can make شهاب and قبس distinct, omit من from من قبس, or annex unlike forms as in ولدار الآخرة خير.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن أضاف أنه جعل الشهاب غير القبس فأضافه أو يكون أراد بشهاب من قبس فأسقط من وأضاف

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r2.claim: With tanwīn, قبس is an adjective agreeing with شهاب.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن نون أنه جعل القبس نعتا لشهاب فأعربه بإعرابه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p269#2/r3.claim: The source explains شهاب as any luminous white thing.

QIRAAT-ER:27:7:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:7:6#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:27:7:6#1/r1.claim: The variant adds fatḥa to the final yāʾ of inniya, changing the suffix's vowel quality without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:27:7:6#1/r1.anchor: Y-iḍ, mutawatir: Variant adds a fatḥa to the final yāʾ (inniya instead of innī)

QIRAAT-ER:27:7:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:7:16#1/r1.speaker: iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:27:7:16#1/r1.claim: The iḍāfa reading makes qabas the second term of “a brand of embers,” rather than an appositive meaning “a brand, a burning one.”
QIRAAT-ER:27:7:16#1/r1.anchor: iḍ, mutawatir: "Variant reads shihābi (genitive construct, iḍāfa) instead of shihābin (tanwīn, apposition)

QIRAAT-ER:27:7:17#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:7:17#1/r1.speaker: iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:27:7:17#1/r1.claim: The same iḍāfa reading makes qabasin the second term of the construct, changing apposition into genitive annexation.
QIRAAT-ER:27:7:17#1/r1.anchor: iḍ, mutawatir: "Same variant as word 16: the iḍāfa reading makes qabasin the second term of a construct phrase

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r1.claim: إذ is most naturally the object of an omitted 'recall': Muhammad is told to recount part of the revelation he received, confirming what precedes. It may instead modify عليم, though Al-Alusi prefers the first analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r1.anchor: منصوب على المفعولية بمضمر خوطب النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وأمر بتلاوة بعض القرءان

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r2.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r2.claim: Al-Bahr objects to making إذ a time adjunct of عليم because that would restrict the attribute to a particular time; Al-Kashf replies that the story's time-setting is not a meaningful restriction and makes the episode evidence for God's knowledge and wisdom generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r2.anchor: وتعقبه في البحر بان ذلك ليس بواضح إذ يصير الوصف مقيدا بالمعمول

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r3.claim: Moses was traveling from Midian near Wadi Tuwa, lost the road on a dark cold night, and saw fire on the side of the Mount after his fire-making failed; he sought news of the route from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r3.anchor: وكان عليه السلام قد حاد عن الطريق في ليلة باردة مظلمة فقدح فاصلد زنده فبدا له من جانب الطور نارا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r4.claim: The 'news' Moses hoped to bring was information about the route, since a traveler approaching a roadside fire would seek directions.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r4.anchor: والمراد بالخبر الذي يأتيهم به من جهة النار الخبر عن حال الطريق

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r5.claim: The future marker may reassure them despite the fire's distance or, preferably, strengthen his promise that he will come even if delayed; its force is not simply to indicate a short wait.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r5.anchor: ولعل الأولى اعتبار كونه للتأكيد ولا يقال : أنه عليه السلام لم يتكلم بالعربية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the future marker is used in promises to affirm that they will surely happen, even when delayed.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r6.anchor: فانها كما ذكره الزمخشري تدخل في الوعد لتأكيده وبيان أنه كائن لامحالة وإن تأخر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r7.claim: Although Moses did not speak Arabic, his original language had an equivalent expression; the Quran's quoted wording represents that meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r7.anchor: مالمانع من أن يكون في غير اللغة العربية ما يؤدي مؤداها بل حكاية القول عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r8.claim: The plural address is honorific if Moses was accompanied only by his wife; calling her his 'family' also reflects the broader sense of household and followers.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r8.anchor: وجمع الضمير إن صح انه لم يكن معه عليه السلام غير امرأته للتعظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r9.claim: A qabas is a flame taken from its source; it can describe شهاب adjectivally or stand in apposition to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r9.anchor: أي بشعلة نار مقبوسة أي ماخوذة من أصلها فقبس صفة شهاب أو بدل منه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r10.speaker: الكوفيون ويعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r10.claim: The Kufans and Yaqub read قبس in the genitive as an adjective or appositive; the other seven readers use genitive annexation, which Abu al-Hasan prefers as an explanatory relation like 'a silk garment.'
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r10.anchor: وهذه قراءة الكوفيين ويعقوب وقرأ باقي السبعة ( بشهاب قبس ) بالاضافة واختارها أبو الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r11.claim: The alternatives express uncertain hopes, so there is no conflict with 20:10; Moses expected at least one of the two outcomes, trusting God not to leave him with neither.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p158#3/r11.anchor: والعدتان على سبيل الظن ولذلك عبر عنهما بصيغة الترجي في سورة طه فلا تدافع بين ما وقع هنا وما وقع هناك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r1.claim: One view says Moses used 'or' because he needed only one outcome: a guide to the road, or, if none appeared, a fire to warm them while they waited.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r1.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن يقال الترديد لأن احتياجه عليه السلام إلى أحدهما لالهما

ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r2.claim: Al-Alusi counters that the reported story has Moses' newborn at the Mount on a freezing, pitch-dark night, with the road lost and livestock scattered, suggesting he needed both; he used 'or' to speak carefully and truthfully.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r2.anchor: قد ورد في القصة أنه عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r3.claim: The phrase expresses hope or purpose that the family warm themselves; صلاء means approaching a fire to heat the body, and can also mean the fire itself, while the vocalized forms distinguish warmth from fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p159/r3.anchor: أي رجاء أو لأجل أن تستدفئوا بها والصلاء بكسر الصاد والمد ويفتح بالقصر الدنو من النار لتسخين البدن

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r1.claim: The opening may mean remember the story when Moses spoke, or attach to ʿalīm.

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r2.claim: Ānastu means that Moses perceived a fire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r2.anchor: إني آنست نارا } أي اذكر قصته

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r3.claim: He promises news about the road because he had lost the way.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r3.anchor: أي عن حال الطريق لأنه قد ضله

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r4.claim: The plural address may be used although his only companion was his wife, since ahl can euphemistically denote a wife.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r4.anchor: وجمع الضمير إن صح أنه لم يكن معه غير امرأته

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r5.claim: The future marker indicates distance and a promise to come even if delayed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r5.anchor: والسين للدلالة على بعد المسافة والوعد بالإتيان وإن أبطأ

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r6.claim: A shihāb qabas is a flame taken from another; the annexation distinguishes it from a flame that is not a brand.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r6.anchor: شعلة نار مقبوسة، وإضافة الشهاب إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r7.speaker: الكوفيون ويعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r7.claim: The Kufans and Yaʿqūb pronounce the nūn in qabasun, making qabas an appositive or description meaning seized.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r7.anchor: ونونه الكوفيون ويعقوب على أن ال { قبس } بدل منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r8.claim: The offers are tentative, as in Ṭā Hā; if Moses obtains neither, he expects at least one by ordinary expectation or trust that God will not combine two deprivations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7/r8.anchor: والعدتان على سبيل الظن ولذلك عبر عنهما بصيغة الترجي في «طه»

BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r1.claim: The preceding description of God as wise and knowing excludes the claim that the Qur’an is human speech or that people can grasp its full depths and imitate it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r1.anchor: { حكيم } أي بالغ الحكمة , فلا شيء من أفعاله إلا وهو في غاية الإتقان { عليم * } أي عظيم العلم واسعة تامة شاملة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r2.claim: The selected stories display divine wisdom and knowledge through contrasting outcomes: distant communities unite in disbelief or faith, families divide, and persistent rebels are swallowed and covered by water.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r2.anchor: فابتدىء بقصة أجمع فيها الأباعد على الكفران فأهلكوا , والأقارب على الإيمان فأنجوا , وثنى بقصة أجمع فيها الباعد على الإيمان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r3.claim: The verb governed by ‘when’ is omitted because its attachment to ‘remember’ is obvious.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r3.anchor: ولما كان تعلق ( إذ ) باذكر من ا لوضوح في حد لا يخفى على أحد ,

BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r4.claim: ‘His family’ means his wife; it is said that she was his only companion on the journey from Midian to Egypt.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r4.anchor: { موسى لأهله } أي زوجة وهو راجع من مدين إلى مصر , قيل : ولم يكن معه غيرها : { إني آنست }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r5.claim: Ānastu means that Moses saw the fire in a way that brought familiarity and dispelled loneliness and fear.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r5.anchor: حصل لي الأنس , وأزال عني الوحسة والنوس

BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r6.claim: The ordered events of the story let people witness God’s perfect wisdom and knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r6.anchor: فعلم بما في هذه القصة من الأفعال المحكمة المنبئة عن تمام العلم اتصافه بالوصفين علما مشاهدا ,

BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r7.claim: The masculine plural expression for ‘family’ lets Moses refer to his wife discreetly and protectively.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r7.anchor: للتعبير عن الزوجة المذكورة بلفظ ( الأهل ) الصالح للمذكر والجمع صيانة لها وسترا .

BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r8.claim: Moses makes a firm promise to bring useful news, whose broad wording can include guidance and suits the sūra’s concern with knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r8.anchor: جازما بالوعد للتعبير بالخير الشامل للهدى وغيره , فكان تعلق الرجاء به أقوى من تعلقه بخصوص كونه هدى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r9.claim: The news might guide them through the darkness because they had lost their way.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r9.anchor: ولعل بعضه يكون مما نهتدي به في هذا الظلام إلى الطريق , وكان قد ضلها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r10.claim: A shihāb is a bright flame; a qabas is a dry branch taken from a larger fire, with fire established in it so it will not go out.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p409/r10.anchor: { أو أتيكم بشهاب } أي شعلة من نار ساطعة { قبس } أي عود جاف مأخوذ من معظم النار فهو بحيث قد استحكمت فيه النار فلا ينطفىء

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r1.speaker: جعفر بن أبي المغيرة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r1.claim: Jaʿfar reports that Moses left his family for forty years at the place where he was called, then went to fulfill God's command.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r1.anchor: عن جعفر بن أبي المغيرة في قوله : اذ قال موسى لاهله اني انست نارا قال : تركهم اربعين سنة في المكان الذي نودي به

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r2.claim: Qatada explains anastu as sensing a fire and says Moses was young when he traveled in God's cause.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : اني انست نارا اني احسست نارا سار في الله حين سار وهو شاب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's account says Moses, after completing his term, lost the way with his family in winter, saw what looked like a fire but was God's light, and told them to wait while he sought news or a firebrand.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r3.anchor: عن السدي ، قال : قال عبد الله بن عباس ، فلما قضى موسى الاجل سار باهله ، فضل الطريق وكان في الشتاء ورفعت له نار

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r4.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r4.claim: The account presents Moses' lost route as the setting for divine honor, prophecy, and speech; he could not kindle a fire until the light appeared.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r4.anchor: فيها موسى بكرامته ، وانباه فيها بنبوته وكلامه ، اخطا فيها الطريق حتى لا يدري اين توجه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r5.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq explains the glowing firebrand as a firebrand with which they could warm themselves.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2842/r5.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق اتيكم بشهاب قبس قال : بقبس تصطلون به

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843/r1.claim: Al-Suddī explains that they might warm themselves against the cold.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843/r1.anchor: عن السدي لعلكم تصطلون قال : من البرد

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843/r2.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843/r2.claim: ʿAmr ibn Maymūn glosses the phrase as finding relief from the cold.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2843/r2.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون قال : لعلكم تصطلون قال : تجدون البرد

BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r1.claim: A person's ahl are those especially close to him; here Moses addresses his wife and those with her in the valley of the Mount.

BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r2.claim: Moses had stayed ten years in Midian with Shuayb, then set out with his family, Shuayb's daughter, for Egypt.
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه مكث بمدين عند شعيب عشر سنين ثم سار بأهله بنت شعيب إلى مصر

BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r3.claim: On a very dark, cold night Moses lost the way; his wife went into labor, his flint failed, and a fire appeared by the Mount, so he told his family to wait.
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r3.anchor: ليلة مظلمة شديدة البرد وقد أخذ امرأته الطلق فقدح فأصلد زنده

BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r4.speaker: التاج
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r4.claim: The Taj glosses īnās as seeing; the root conveys something's appearance and what departs from estrangement.
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r4.anchor: قال في "التاج" : (الإيناس : ديدن) والباب يدل على ظهور الشيء

BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r5.speaker: مقاتل
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r5.claim: Muqatil says the fire was light, the light of the Lord of Might, seen Friday night at the mountain's right side in the Holy Land; the manifestation of light as fire was discussed in Sura Taha.
BURSEVI:v6p233#3/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل : النار هو النور وهو نور رب العزة رآه ليلة الجمعة عن يمين الجبل بالأرض المقدسة

BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r1.claim: The future prefix can indicate the distance of the road, or reinforce the promise that Moses will come even if delayed.
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r1.anchor: والسين للدلالة على بعد المسافة أو لتحقيق الوعد بالإتيان وإن أبطأ فيكون للتأكيد

BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r2.claim: Moses promises to bring news of the route from someone near the fire, or to return with a flame if no guide is there.
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r2.anchor: أي بشعلة نار مقبوسة أي مأخوذة من معظم النار ومن أصلها إن لم أجد عندها من يدلني على الطريق

BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r3.claim: A shihāb is a bright flame and a qabaṣ is something taken from it; iqtabās is seeking it, later used for seeking knowledge and guidance.
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r3.anchor: الشهاب الشعلة الساطعة من النار المتوقدة والقبس المتناول من الشعلة

BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r4.claim: The idiom اقتبست منه نارا وعلما means taking fire from someone and, by extension, receiving knowledge from them.
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r4.anchor: يقال : اقتبست منه نارا وعلما استفدته منه

BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r5.claim: There is no contradiction with Moses' hopeful wording in 20:10: a person with strong hope may speak confidently while allowing events could turn otherwise.
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r5.anchor: لا تدافع لأن الراجي إذا قوي رجاؤه يقول : سأفعل كذا مع تجويزه خلاف ذلك

BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r6.claim: Moses hopes his family can warm themselves against the cold with the fire.

BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r7.claim: Ṣilāʾ denotes a great fire, and iṣṭilāʾ is warming oneself by it.
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r7.anchor: والصلاء النار العظيمة والاصطلاء (كرم شدن بآتش)

BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r8.claim: Some say warming oneself by fire hardens the heart, and no report says the Prophet warmed himself at a fire.
BURSEVI:v6p233#4/r8.anchor: قال بعضهم : الاصطلاء بالنار يقسي القلب ولم يرو أنه عليه السلام اصطلى بالنار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r1.claim: The cited poetry uses qabs for a flame or firebrand taken from fire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r1.anchor: في كفة صعدة مشقفة ... فيها سنان كشعلة القبس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r2.claim: A shihab originally means a shooting star pursuing an eavesdropper; other luminous objects are called one by analogy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r2.anchor: وأصل الشهاب الكوكب المنقض في أثر مسترق السمع وكل من يقال له شهاب من المنيرات فعلى التشبيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says any white luminous thing is a shihab; Ibn Atiyya objects to this claim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: كل أبيض ذي نور فهو شهاب وكلامه معترض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.claim: Qabs may be a noun, meaning a flame I acquired, or an adjective in an annexation like dar al-akhira.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.anchor: و «القبس» يحتمل أن يكون اسما غير صفة ويحتمل أن يكون صفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور والحسن وأهل المدينة ومكة والشام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.claim: These readers use annexation, شهاب قبس.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بإضافة «شهاب» إلى «قبس» وهي قراءة الحسن وأهل المدينة ومكة والشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.claim: They read شهاب with tanwin, making قبس an adjective.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي «بشهاب قبس» بتنوين «شهاب» فهذا على الصفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.claim: Qabs may also be the verbal noun of qabasa yaqbas, as jalb is of jalaba yajlib.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون «القبس» مصدر قبس يقبس كما الجلب مصدر جلب يجلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Hasan considers annexation better and more common in recitation, like dar ajur and suwar dhahab.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن: الإضافة أجود وأكثر في القراءة كما تقول دار آجر وسوار ذهب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r9.claim: Taṣṭalūn means to warm themselves against the cold.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r10.claim: The pronoun in جاءها refers to the fire Moses saw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249#2/r10.anchor: والضمير في جاءها للنار التي رآها موسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r1.claim: The opening means: remember when Moses said to his family.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ إذ قال موسى ﴾ المعنى أذكر أذ قال موسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب إلا زيدا
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r2.claim: These readers pronounce shihābin with tanwīn; the remaining readers use an unmarked construct phrase.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r2.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب إلا زيدا بشهاب بالتنوين وقرأالباقون على الإضافة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r3.claim: With tanwīn, qabas is an adjective describing the luminous flame; any white, radiant thing can be called a shihāb.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج من نون الشهاب وجعل القبس من صفة الشهاب وكل أبيض ذي نور فهو شهاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r4.claim: Al-Farra says the construct phrase is an instance of a noun being annexed to itself under different names, as in 12:109.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r4.anchor: هذا مما يضاف إلى نفسه إذا اختلفت الاسماء كقوله ﴿ ولدار الآخرة ﴾ يوسف 109

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba says shihāb means fire and qabas is fire that has been kindled, or the kindled brand itself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r5.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة الشهاب النار والقبس النار تقبس يقال قبست النار قبسا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r6.claim: Taṣṭalūn means to warm yourselves; the season was winter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p154#5/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ تصطلون ﴾ أي تستدفئون وكان الزمان شتاء

JISHUMI:v8p5405/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r6.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r6.claim: These readers leave shihāb indefinite and make qabas its adjective, meaning luminous.
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r6.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب: بشهاب قبس منونة غير مضاف، جعل قبسا صفة،

JISHUMI:v8p5405/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r7.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r7.claim: Others use genitive iḍāfa, understood as a flame of fire; Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim prefer it.
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r7.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بشهاب بغير تنوين مضاف إلى قبس فالأول على تقدير منور،

JISHUMI:v8p5405/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r8.claim: Īnās is sensing something by a reassuring or familiar means.
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r8.anchor: الإحساس بالشيء من جهة يؤنس بها، آنسته أونسه إيناسا.

JISHUMI:v8p5405/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r9.claim: A shihāb is a column-like firelight and can name a streaking star.
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r9.anchor: والشهاب: نور كالعمود من النار، وجمعه: شهب، ومنه قيل للنجم الذي يمتد في السماء: شهاب.

JISHUMI:v8p5405/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r10.claim: Qabas is a piece or flame taken from fire, borrowed for acquiring knowledge.
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r10.anchor: والقبس: القطعة من النار، واقتبس من النار اقتباسا؛ أي: أخذ منها شعلة، واقتبس علما مشبه به.

JISHUMI:v8p5405/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r11.claim: Iṣṭilāʾ means seeking warmth from fire.
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r11.anchor: واقتبس علما مشبه به. والاصطلاء: طلب التدفؤ بالنار.

JISHUMI:v8p5405/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r13.claim: One explanation says Moses addresses his wife as a group.
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r13.anchor: وقول موسى لأهله: (آتيكم) قيل: لأنه أقامها مقام الجماعة،

JISHUMI:v8p5405/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r14.claim: Another explanation says others of her children were with her.
JISHUMI:v8p5405/r14.anchor: وقيل: كان معها غيرها من أولادها.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r1.claim: Idh is governed by remember; the narrative invites reflection on God's wisdom and knowledge through Moses' story.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r1.anchor: منصوب باذكر كأنه قال على أثر ذلك خذ من آثار حكمته وعلمه قصة موسى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r2.claim: Moses addresses his wife and companions travelling from Midian toward Egypt.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r2.anchor: لزوجته ومن معه عند مسير ممن مدين إلى مصر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r3.claim: Anastu means I saw; Moses had lost the route and expected news about the way from the fire.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r3.anchor: عن حال الطريق لأنه كان قد ضله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r4.claim: Kufans nunate both words, making qabas an apposition or adjective for a flame; others use a construct phrase, since a flame may or may not be a brand.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r4.anchor: بالتنوين كوفي أي شعلة مضيئة قبس نار مقبوسة بدل أو صفة وغيرهم بشهاب قبس على الإضافة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r5.claim: The promise does not conflict with Moses' more tentative wording in al-Qasas: strong hope can be expressed as certainty while allowing failure.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r5.anchor: ولعلى آتيكم في القصص مع أن أحدهما زج والآخر تيقن لأن الراجي إذا قوي رجاؤه يقول سأفعل كذا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r6.claim: The future tense assures his family he will bring something even if delayed; the alternative means he expected either directions or fire, not necessarily both.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r6.anchor: ومجيئه بسين التسويف عدة لأهله أنه يأتيهم به وأن أبطأ أو كانت المسافة بعيدة وبأو لأنه بني الرجاء على أنه إن لم يظفر بحاجته جميعا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r7.claim: Different wording for the same story supports transmitting hadith by meaning and the validity of marriage without the explicit formula I marry you.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r7.anchor: واختلاف الألفاظ في هاتين الصورتين والقصة واحدة دليل عن جواز نقل الحديث بالمعنى وجواز النكاح بغير لفظ التزوج

NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r8.claim: Tastalun means warm yourselves by the fire against the cold; the ta changes because of the preceding sad.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p204#2/r8.anchor: تستدفئون بالنار من البرد الذي أصابكم والطاء بدل من تاء افتعل لأجل الصاد

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r1.claim: Idh is governed by an omitted udhkur; Muḥammad is told to recall Moses' story after the statement that revelation comes from the Wise and Knowing.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r1.anchor: خذ يا محمد من آثار حكمته وعلمه قصة موسى

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r2.claim: Ānastu nāran means Moses saw a fire from a distance.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r2.anchor: { إني آنست نارا } أي أبصرتها من بعد.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r3.speaker: الحارث بن حلزة
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r3.claim: Al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza's verse uses ānastu to mean perceiving or seeing.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r3.anchor:
قال الحارث بن حلزة:
آنست نبأة وأفزعها

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r4.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r4.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read shihābin with tanwīn, making qabas separate.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r4.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: { بشهاب قبس } بتنوين { شهاب }.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r5.claim: The remaining readers omit tanwīn and use iḍāfa; Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim prefer this reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r5.anchor: والباقون بغير تنوين على الإضافة أي بشعلة نار واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r6.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ defends iḍāfa as joining different names for one thing, as in dār al-ākhira and masjid al-jāmiʿ.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r6.anchor: وزعم الفراء في ترك التنوين أنه بمنزلة قولهم: ولدار الآخرة، ومسجد الجامع، وصلاة الأولى يضاف الشيء إلى نفسه إذا اختلفت أسماؤه.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r7.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r7.claim: Al-Naḥḥās rejects adding a word to itself; he explains this as a type-to-genus iḍāfa, like a silk garment or iron ring.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r7.anchor: قال النحاس: إضافة الشيء إلى نفسه محال عند البصريين، لأن معنى الإضافة في اللغة ضم شيء إلى شيء فمحال أن يضم الشيء إلى نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r8.claim: Shihāb is anything luminous, such as a star or burning stick; qabas names an ember or firebrand, so the phrase means a flame from a firebrand.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r8.anchor: والشهاب كل ذي نور نحو الكوكب والعود الموقد. والقبس اسم لما يقتبس من جمر وما أشبهه فالمعنى بشهاب من قبس.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r9.claim: Qabas is the noun for what is taken from fire, from aqbasa; the noun follows the pattern of qabḍ from qabaḍa.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r9.anchor: يقال: أقبست قبسا والاسم قبس. كما تقول: قبضت قبضا. والاسم القبض.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r10.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r10.claim: Al-Mahdawī says qabas after tanwīn can be a substitute or adjective; iḍāfa is better if qabas is a noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r10.anchor: المهدوي: أو صفة له لأن القبس يجوز أن يكون اسما غير صفة، ويجوز أن يكون صفة

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r11.claim: The iḍāfa, when qabas is a noun, expresses a type related to its genus; an uncanonical accusative could be apposition or circumstantial.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r11.anchor: والإضافة فيه إذا كان غير صفة أحسن. وهي إضافة النوع إلى جنسه كخاتم فضة وشبهه. ولو قرىء بنصب قبس على البيان أو الحال كان أحسن.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r12.claim: In taṣṭalūn the original tāʾ changes to ṭāʾ to harmonize with emphatic ṣād; the word means to warm yourselves from the cold.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:7/r12.anchor: أصل الطاء تاء فأبدل منها هنا طاء لأن الطاء مطبقة والصاد مطبقة فكان الجمع بينهما حسنا، ومعناه يستدفئون من البرد.

QASHANI:27:4-7/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:4-7/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:4-7/r6.claim: Moses is the heart, his family the soul and outer and inner senses; his order to wait means remain still and do not disturb his moment with activity.

QASHANI:27:4-7/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:4-7/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:4-7/r7.claim: Moses perceives with the eye of insight the fire of the active intellect and seeks knowledge of the path to God, which he had lost while tending animal powers and the animal soul.
QASHANI:27:4-7/r7.anchor: بعين البصيرة { نارا } أي: نار وما أعظمها هي نار العقل والفعال

QASHANI:27:4-7/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:4-7/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:4-7/r8.claim: Alternatively, he brings a luminous flame from his contact with the intellect; its warmth frees his family from bodily attachment and stirs longing for the divine gardens and love's journey to the breast.
QASHANI:27:4-7/r8.anchor: بشعلة نورية تشرق عليكم حين اتصالي بالنار وتنوري بها

RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r2.claim: The opening “when” is governed by an omitted imperative, “remember,” though it may instead depend on “Knowing.”
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r2.anchor: منصوب بمضمر وهو اذكر كأنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r3.claim: Calling his wife “his family” implies that she alone accompanied Moses; this explains the later plural address, “stay here.”
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r3.anchor: على أنه لم يكن مع موسى عليه السلام غير امرأته

RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r4.claim: They were traveling by night in cold weather and had lost the way; seeing a distant fire reassured them with hope of directions and warmth.

RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r5.claim: One reported sense of “I perceived a fire” is that Moses saw or beheld it.

RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r6.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r6.claim: Another reported sense is that Moses came upon or found the fire and felt familiar with it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون بل المراد صادفت ووجدت فآنست به

RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r7.claim: Rāzī prefers “saw,” since Arabic speakers do not distinguish “I perceived with my eye” from “I saw with my eye.”
RAZI-FULL:v24p155/r7.anchor: لأنهم لا يفرقون بين قول القائل آنست ببصري

STUDYQURAN:27:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r1.speaker: Sufi commentators
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r1.claim: Sufi interpretation maps conceptual knowledge of fire, seeing it, and being consumed by it to theoretical knowledge, direct vision, and the soul's transformation by the Truth.
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r1.anchor: the levels of certainty envisioned as progressive stages in the spiritual life

STUDYQURAN:27:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r2.claim: R says family may refer only to Moses' wife, one possible meaning of ahl.
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r2.anchor: to refer to Moses’ wife only, which is one possible meaning of ahl (R)

STUDYQURAN:27:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r3.speaker: IK, R
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r3.claim: IK and R understand the news as information about the road, since Moses and his party had become lost.
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r3.anchor: Some news refers to information about the road, since they had become lost on their journey (IK, R)

STUDYQURAN:27:7/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:7/r4.claim: The episode is compared with 28:29 and Exodus 3:1–6.

TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r3.claim: The temporal إذ clause is attached to عليم: God knew when Moses said this.
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r3.anchor: وإذ من صلة عليم. ومعنى الكلام

TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r4.claim: Moses was traveling from Midian to Egypt; the night’s cold troubled his family as his flint failed to spark.
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r4.anchor: وهو في مسيره من مدين إلى مصر، وقد آذاهم برد ليلهم

TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r5.claim: آنست means that Moses saw or sensed a fire, then told his family to stay where they were.
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r5.anchor: أي أبصرت نارا أو أحسستها، فامكثوا مكانكم

TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r6.claim: Moses would bring news from the fire; the suffix in منها refers back to the fire.
TAB-FULL:v18p7#4/r6.anchor: يعني من النار، والهاء والألف من ذكر النار.

TAB-FULL:v18p8/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r1.speaker: قراء المدينة والبصرة
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r1.claim: Medinan and Basran readers annex قَبَس to شهاب without tanwin, meaning a flame from which Moses would take fire.
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r1.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان معروفتان في قراءة الأمصار، متقاربتا المعنى، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب

TAB-FULL:v18p8/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r2.speaker: قراء أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r2.claim: Kufan readers use tanwin on شهاب without annexation, meaning a flame that has been taken from the fire.
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r2.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان معروفتان في قراءة الأمصار، متقاربتا المعنى، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب

TAB-FULL:v18p8/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r3.claim: Both established regional readings are close in meaning, and either one is correct.
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r3.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان معروفتان في قراءة الأمصار، متقاربتا المعنى، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب

TAB-FULL:v18p8/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r4.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r4.claim: A Basran grammarian says an appositional قَبَس requires tanwin, while annexation to it leaves شهاب uninflected.
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r4.anchor: وكان بعض نحويي البصرة يقول: إذا جعل القبس بدلا من الشهاب فالتنوين في الشهاب

TAB-FULL:v18p8/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r5.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r5.claim: A Kufan grammarian allows annexation like ولدار الآخرة, where differing names and forms make the second seem distinct; he also cites حبة الخضراء and ليلة القمراء.
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r5.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: إذا أضيف الشهاب إلى القبس فهو بمنزلة قوله {ولدار الآخرة} [يوسف: 109] مما يضاف إلى نفسه

TAB-FULL:v18p8/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r6.speaker: آخر من نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r6.claim: Another Kufan grammarian says annexation is unsuitable if قَبَس is the same as شهاب or an adjective, though rare usage and verses provide exceptions.
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r6.anchor: وقال آخر منهم: إن كان الشهاب هو القبس لم تجز الإضافة، لأن القبس نعت

TAB-FULL:v18p8/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r7.claim: When the flame and the taken fire are distinct, annexation fits; ordinary Arabic avoids annexing a noun to itself or its adjective.
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r7.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أن الشهاب إذا أريد به أنه غير القبس فالقراءة فيه بالإضافة

TAB-FULL:v18p8/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r8.claim: If شهاب means the very قَبَس or describes it, tanwin is correct because Arabic normally avoids annexing a noun to itself or its adjective.
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r8.anchor: وإذا أريد بالشهاب أنه هو القبس، أو أنه نعت له، فالصواب في الشهاب التنوين

TAB-FULL:v18p8/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r9.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r9.claim: The poet’s image of a spearhead like the flame of a قَبَس illustrates treating the flame and the taken fire as distinct.
TAB-FULL:v18p8/r9.anchor: في كفه صعدة مشقفة … فيها سنان كشعلة القبس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r1.claim: Idh is in the accusative, meaning recall when Moses said, that is, recall his story.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: موضع (إذ) نصب، المعنى: اذكر {إذ قال موسى}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r2.claim: His household here means his wife.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r3.claim: The explanation of Moses noticing a fire is given earlier in Sūrat Ṭā Hā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r3.anchor: {إني آنست نارا} مفسر في سورة: طه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r4.claim: Khabar means information about the road; Moses had become confused and left the route.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r4.anchor: أين الطريق، أي: بخبر عن الطريق؛ وقد كان تحير، وترك الطريق. قاله ابن عباس ومقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r5.claim: If Moses found no one to tell him the road, he would bring his family a firebrand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r5.anchor: أي: فإن لم أجد أحدا يخبرني عن الطريق {آتيكم بشهاب قبس}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r6.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r6.claim: A shihāb is a stick containing fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r6.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: الشهاب: العود الذي فيه نار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r7.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r7.claim: A shihāb is the end of a piece of wood with a blazing fire in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161/r7.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم: الشهاب: أصل خشبة فيها نار ساطعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r1.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r1.claim: A shihāb is a blazing flame; its plurals are shuhub and shuhbān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r1.anchor: وقال الليث: الشهاب شعلة نار ساطعة، والجمع: الشهب والشهبان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r2.claim: Anything white and luminous can be called a shihāb, including a star, fire, or spearhead.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: كل أبيض ذي نور فهو شهاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī says he cannot tell whether al-Zajjāj's definition is transmitted or an inference.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو علي: الذي قاله أبو إسحاق لا أدري أقاله رواية أم استدلالا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r4.claim: The phrase is read with tanwīn or in annexation: al-Zajjāj takes qabas as an adjective, while al-Farrāʾ explains annexation as a noun added to a different name, as in 12:109.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r5.claim: Qabas may be an adjective or a noun for what is taken or kindled; if adjectival, tanwīn is preferable because a described noun is not normally annexed to its adjective.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r5.anchor: إذا كان قوله: (قبس) صفة فالأحسن التنوين؛ لأن الموصوف لا يضاف إلى صفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r6.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan considers annexation the more frequent and better reading, comparing it to a brick house or a gold bracelet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن: الإضافة أكثر وأجود في القراءة كما تقول: دار آجر، وسوار ذهب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r7.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī notes that Abū al-Ḥasan treats qabas as a noun, like brick or gold, rather than as an adjective.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: فأبو الحسن: جعل القبس غير صفة، ألا ترى أنه جعله بمنزلة الآجر والذهب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r8.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r8.claim: The commentators explain qabas here as a flame of fire.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r9.claim: They sought the fire so they could warm themselves against the cold; al-Kalbī says it was the depth of winter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r9.anchor: {لعلكم تصطلون} لكي تصطلوا، من البرد (¬5). قال الكلبي: وكان ذلك في شدة الشتاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r10.claim: Ṣalā bi-l-nār and iṣṭalā bihā mean to get warm by a fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r10.anchor: ويقال: صلى بالنار واصطلى بها إذا استدفأ.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r11.claim: The full interpretation of this verse was already given in Sūrat Ṭā Hā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r11.anchor: واستقصاء تفسير هذه الآية قد تقدم في سورة طه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r12.claim: The detailed explanation of qabas was already given in Sūrat Ṭā Hā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p161#2/r12.anchor: وتفسير القبس قد سبق في سورة طه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r7.claim: Qatadah glosses Moses' words as “I sensed a fire.”

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r8.claim: In 20:10 Moses saw what appeared to him as fire, though it was actually light; al-Suddi likewise glosses this as seeing a light.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r8.anchor: وقال في آية أخرى: {إذ رأى نارا} [طه: 10] رآها نارا عند نفسه، وإنما كانت نورا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r9.claim: Moses would bring news of the road because the family was off the route.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r9.anchor: {سآتيكم منها بخبر} [النمل: 7] الطريق، وكان على غير طريق.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r10.claim: Moses' hope of finding guidance by the fire in 20:10 means finding guides who would show the road.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p533/r10.anchor: وقال في آية أخرى: {أو أجد على النار هدى} [طه: 10] ، أي: هداة يهدون إلى الطريق

MAJAZ:v2p92/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p92/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p92/r2.claim: Ānastu means I saw and sensed the fire.
MAJAZ:v2p92/r2.anchor: إني آنست نارا» (7) أي أبصرت وأحسست بها..

MAJAZ:v2p92/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p92/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p92/r3.claim: A shihāb qabas is a flame; qabas is a live ember taken from a fire, as the poem’s ‘flame of al-qabas’ illustrates.
MAJAZ:v2p92/r3.anchor: بشهاب قبس» (7) أي بشعلة نار، ومجاز «قبس» ما اقتبست منها من الجمر قال:

ITQAN:v2p353/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p353/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p353/r7.claim: The text glosses شهاب قبس as a flame from which fire is taken, citing Tarafa b. al-Abd as evidence of Arab usage.
ITQAN:v2p353/r7.anchor: قال شعلة من نار يقتبسون منه قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال نعم أما سمعت قول طرفة بن العبد

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r1.claim: Moses had lost the road; the passage omits that he saw the fire and turned toward it, then spoke to his family to guide their way.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r1.anchor: فالخبر ما يخبر به عن حال الطريق لأنه كان قد ضل

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r2.claim: Shihāb is a flame, and qabas is fire taken from another fire; shihāb is annexed to qabas because it may be a firebrand or something else.

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r3.claim: With tanwīn, qabas is analyzed as an apposition or adjective, since the preceding word already conveys the sense of taking fire.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r3.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتنوين جعل القبس بدلا أو صفة لما فيه من معنى القبس

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r4.claim: The hopeful wording does not conflict with the report that Moses had completed his term: a person with strong hope may say something will happen while still allowing failure.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r4.anchor: قد يقول الراجي إذا قوي رجاؤه سأفعل كذا وسيكون كذا مع تجويزه الخيبة

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r5.claim: The future particle is a promise to his family that he will bring something back, even if he is delayed or the way is distant.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r5.anchor: جوابه : عدة منه لأهله أنه يأتيهم به وإن أبطأ أو كانت المسافة بعيدة

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r6.claim: “Or” expresses his hope to obtain at least one of the two things—directions or fire—relying on God’s custom not to deprive a servant of both.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r6.anchor: بنى الرجاء على أنه إن لم يظفر بهذين المقصودين ظفر بأحدهما

RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r7.claim: The phrase means “so that you may warm yourselves,” implying that they needed a fire because it was cold.
RAZI-FULL:v24p155#2/r7.anchor: فالمعنى لكي تصطلون وذلك يدل على حاجة بهم إلى الاصطلاء

TABATABAI:27:7-8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r1.claim: The five stories exemplify the sūra's opening promise and warning: promise predominates in the first three accounts of Moses, David, and Solomon, while warning predominates in the last two.
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r1.anchor: بيان أول القصص الخمس التي أشير إليها في السورة استشهادا لما في صدرها من التبشير والإنذار

TABATABAI:27:7-8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r2.claim: Moses's family here is his wife, whom al-Qasas identifies as Shuʿayb's daughter; al-Majmaʿ says the plural “I see you” addresses her as company in a lonely place, though others may also have accompanied them.
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r2.anchor: المراد بأهله امرأته وهي بنت شعيب على ما ذكره الله تعالى في سورة القصص

TABATABAI:27:7-8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r3.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r3.claim: Al-Majmaʿ al-Bayān glosses anastu as seeing, or as sensing something in a way that brings reassurance.
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r3.anchor: وفي المجمع الإيناس الإبصار، وقيل آنست أي أحسست بالشيء من جهة يؤنس بها

TABATABAI:27:7-8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r4.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r4.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines a shihāb as a column-like flame or extended light and qabas as a flame-brand taken from a fire; al-Iṣfahānī also calls shihāb a bright flame or atmospheric phenomenon.
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r4.anchor: والشهاب على ما في المجمع نور كالعمود من النار وكل نور يمتد كالعمود يسمى شهابا

TABATABAI:27:7-8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r5.claim: Iṣṭilāʾ means warming oneself by a fire.

TABATABAI:27:7-8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r6.claim: Moses and his family had lost their way and were cold on a dark night; he saw a distant fire and planned to ask for directions or bring back a brand to warm them.
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r6.anchor: أنه كان حينذاك يسير بأهله وقد ضل الطريق وأصابه وأهله البرد في ليلة داجية

TABATABAI:27:7-8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r7.claim: The fire seems to have appeared only to Moses: if the others had seen it too, the wording would point to it rather than introduce it indefinitely.
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r7.anchor: ويظهر من السياق أيضا أن النار إنما ظهرت له عليه السلام ولم يشاهدها غيره

TABATABAI:27:7-8/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r8.claim: The verb “come” is repeated because Moses names two different possible returns: information or a firebrand.
TABATABAI:27:7-8/r8.anchor: ولعل اختلاف الإتيان بالخبر والإتيان بالنار نوعا هو الموجب لتكرار لفظ الإتيان

TABRISI:27:3-8/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r12.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:27:3-8/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj says إذ is governed by an omitted أذكر, meaning remember the story of Moses when he spoke to his family.
TABRISI:27:3-8/r12.anchor: قال الزجاج: العامل في إذ أذكر أي أذكر في قصة موسى إذ قال لأهله

TABRISI:27:3-8/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r13.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:27:3-8/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj identifies Moses's family member here as his wife, the daughter of Shuayb.

TABRISI:27:3-8/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:3-8/r14.claim: Ānastu means I saw or perceived; the word ins is related to humans being visible.

TABRISI:27:3-8/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:3-8/r15.claim: An alternative sense is perceiving something in a way that brings familiarity and reassurance; what one senses this way is perceived with calmness toward it.
TABRISI:27:3-8/r15.anchor: وقيل: آنست أي أحسست بالشيء من جهة يؤنس بها وما آنست به فقد أحسست به مع سكون نفسك إليه

TABRISI:27:3-8/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:3-8/r16.claim: Moses tells them to stay while he seeks route information from the fire, hoping to find their way since they had lost it.
TABRISI:27:3-8/r16.anchor: معناه فالزموا مكانكم لعلي آتيكم من هذه النار بخبر الطريق وأهتدي بها إلى الطريق

TABRISI:27:3-8/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:3-8/r17.claim: A shihāb qabas is a flame; shihāb is light shaped like a column, and any extended column of light may be called one.
TABRISI:27:3-8/r17.anchor: أي بشعلة نار والشهاب نور كالعمود من النار وكل نور يمتد مثل العمود يسمى شهابا

TABRISI:27:3-8/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:3-8/r18.claim: Moses addresses his wife with a plural pronoun by treating her as a group, since he felt familiarity and safety with her in the desolate place.
TABRISI:27:3-8/r18.anchor: وإنما قال لامرأته آتيكم على لفظ خطاب الجمع لأنه أقامه مقام الجماعة في الأنس بها والسكون إليها

TABRISI:27:3-8/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:3-8/r19.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TABRISI:27:3-8/r19.claim: The purpose was to let them warm themselves; Hasan and Qatada say they had been struck by cold while traveling in winter.
TABRISI:27:3-8/r19.anchor: أي لكي تستدفئوا بها وذلك لأنهم كانوا قد أصابهم البرد وكانوا شاتين عن الحسن وقتادة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r6.claim: Moses was traveling from Midian toward Egypt with his family, lost the way, and saw a fire at a distance.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r6.anchor: في مسيرة من مدين إلى مصر، وقد ضل الطريق، وأصلد زنده

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r7.claim: Moses hoped to learn the route from the fire.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r8.claim: A burning brand is a flame he could take for them so they could warm themselves.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:4-8/r8.anchor: شعلة نار أقتبسها لكم { لعلكم تصطلون } تستدفئون من البرد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r1.claim: A flame-brand is a piece from the base of a tree, also called a glowing ember in 28:29.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r1.anchor: {أو آتيكم بشهاب قبس} [النمل: 7] وقال في آية أخرى: {أو جذوة من النار} [القصص: 29] وهو أصل الشجرة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p534/r2.claim: The purpose is that they might warm themselves.

ELMALILI:27:7-8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r1.claim: Moses was traveling from Midian with his family, lost on a cold dark night in the Tuwa valley, could not strike a spark, and saw a fire toward Mount Ṭūr when all means had failed.
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r1.anchor: ehliyle Medyen’den çıkmış giderken Tuvâ vadisinde soğuk ve karanlık bir gecede yolu şaşırmış, çakmak çakmış taşı çakmamış

ELMALILI:27:7-8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r2.claim: He tells his family he sensed a fire and hopes to bring news or a flame so they can warm themselves; these were their two needs.
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r2.anchor: Demek ki bütün ihtiyaç bu ikinin birinde toplanıyordu: Yoldan bir haber almak veya bir ocak yakmak

ELMALILI:27:7-8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r3.claim: News is mentioned first because it is a spiritual or otherworldly aim, while kindling a fire for warmth serves a worldly aim.
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r3.anchor: haber uhrevî, ocak yakıp ısınmak dünyevî bir gaye olduğu için olmalı ki haberi takdim etmiştir.

ELMALILI:27:7-8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r4.claim: The concise wording conveys profound inspirations that cannot be contained in ordinary exegesis and exposition.
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r4.anchor: bu veciz ifadeden tefsir ve beyâna sığamayacak[^1] pek derin ilhamlar duyulur.

ELMALILI:27:7-8/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r5.claim: Using ‘you all’ instead of ‘you’ shows that Moses meant more than a single member of his family.
ELMALILI:27:7-8/r5.anchor: “Sana” demeyip “size” demesi ehlinden yalnız bir ferd kastedilmediğini anlatır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r1.claim: The account appears elsewhere with different occasions and styles, including in al-Aʿraf, Ta Ha, and al-Qasas; this episode occurred on a cold night as Moses traveled from Midian to Egypt with his family.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r1.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ’nın kıssası çeşitli yerlerde çeşitli vesilelerle anlatılmaktadır. Burada anlatılanlar biraz daha genişçe ve farklı üslûplarla A‘râf

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r2.claim: Commentators say the light Moses took for fire was actually divine light.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:7/r2.anchor: Müfessirler, Hz. Mûsâ’nın ateş sandığı ışığın gerçekte ilâhî bir nur olduğunu belirtirler

NAHHAS:v3p197/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p197/r9.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v3p197/r9.claim: The Kufans read the construction without tanwin; the Medinans and Abu Amr read it with tanwin.

NAHHAS:v3p197/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p197/r10.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p197/r10.claim: Al-Farra explains the uninflected form as a self-annexation of one name to another, like ولدار الآخرة.
NAHHAS:v3p197/r10.anchor: فزعم الفراء في ترك التنوين أنه بمنزلة قولهم

NAHHAS:v3p197/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p197/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p197/r11.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects self-annexation as impossible; he prefers an annexation of kind to material, like ثوب خز, while the tanwin reading treats قبس as apposition.
NAHHAS:v3p197/r11.anchor: قال أبو جعفر إضافة الشيء إلى نفسه محال عند البصريين لأن معنى الإضافة في اللغة

NAHHAS:v3p197/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p197/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p197/r12.claim: A شهاب is anything luminous, such as a star or burning stick; قبس is a name for a live coal taken from fire.
NAHHAS:v3p197/r12.anchor: والشهاب كل ذي نور نحو الكوكب والعود الموقد والقبس اسم لما يقتبس من جمر

NAHHAS:v3p197/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p197/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p197/r13.claim: The root's tā was replaced by emphatic ط because it meets the emphatic ص.
NAHHAS:v3p197/r13.anchor: أصل الطاء تاء فأبدل منها طاء لأن الطاء مطبقة والصاد مطبقة
