ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r2.claim: إذ is accusative; recall Moses speaking to his family, that is, recall his story.
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r2.anchor: المعنى اذكر إذ قال موسى لأهله

ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r3.claim: آنست نارا means Moses saw a fire.

ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r4.claim: قبس is read with tanwin or in annexation; with tanwin it describes شهاب, since every luminous white thing is a flame.
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r4.anchor: وكل أبيض ذي نور فهو شهاب

ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r5.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r5.claim: Exegetical reports say they were in winter and needed the fire to warm themselves.
ZAJJAJ:v4p108/r5.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنهم كانوا في شتاء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r6.speaker: الأخفش
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r6.claim: Kufan readers ʿAsim, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi mark shihāb with tanwin; the others do not, as qabs may be appositional or genitive, both acceptable to al-Akhfash.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p369/r6.anchor: قال الأخفش في (معاني القرآن: آية النمل 7)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r6.claim: Samarrai observes that every sura beginning with ṭā gives a detailed account of Moses near its beginning, unlike other suras opened by disconnected letters.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r6.anchor: كل سورة تبدأ بالطاء ترد فيه قصة موسى في أوائلها مفصلة قبل سائر القصص

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p99/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p99/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p99/r3.claim: The parallel accounts of Moses finding a fire vary in wording: al-Naml mentions a firebrand, while al-Qasas says a firewood ember and includes his instruction to wait.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p99/r3.anchor: سآتيكم منها بخبر أو آتيكم بشهاب قبس لعلكم تصطلون

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r1.claim: The Naml account says Musa perceived a fire; al-Qaṣaṣ adds that it was from the side of the mountain.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r1.anchor: النمل القصص {إني آنَسْتُ نَاراً} {آنَسَ مِن جَانِبِ الطور نَاراً}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r2.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds Musa's instruction for his family to stay while he goes to the fire; the comparison lists this detail as absent from Naml.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r3.claim: Naml uses a definite promise that Musa will bring news, while al-Qaṣaṣ phrases it as a hope or possibility.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r4.claim: The Naml wording specifies a burning brand, while al-Qaṣaṣ speaks more generally of a firebrand.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r4.anchor: {أَوْ آتِيكُمْ بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ} {أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ النار}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p112/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p112/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p112/r3.claim: The more specific idkhāl pairs with the more specific shihāb qabas, while the broader sulūk pairs with the broader jadwah.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p112/r3.anchor: وناسب أن يوضع الإدخال، وهو أخص من السلوك مع (الشهاب القبس) الذي هو أخَصُّ من الجذوة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r2.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds the location on the mountain's side because that sūra develops the scene in greater detail.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r2.anchor: فزاد {مِن جَانِبِ الطور} وذلك لمقامِ التفصيلِ الذي بُنيت عليه القصة في سورة القصص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r3.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds Musa's instruction to his family to stay, another detail suited to its expanded narrative rather than Naml's concise account.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r3.anchor: بزيادة {امكثوا} . وهذه الزيادة نظيرة ما ذكرناه آنفاً أعني مناسبة لمقامِ التفصيل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r4.claim: Musa's fear in al-Qaṣaṣ makes his promise tentative (perhaps he will bring news); Naml's less fearful, confident scene uses the definite promise that he will return.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r4.anchor: فبنى الكلام في النمل على القطع {سَآتِيكُمْ} وفي القصص على الترجي {لعلي آتِيكُمْ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r2.claim: Qasas adds the location من جانب الطور because its retelling favors detail, unlike the concise Naml account.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r2.anchor: وذلك لمقام التفصيل الذي بنيت عليه القصة في سورة القصص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r3.claim: Qasas also adds امكثوا, another detail suited to its expanded telling, whereas the Naml story is built on brevity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r3.anchor: بزيادة "امْكُثُوا". وهذه الزيادة نظيرة ما ذكرناه آنفا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r4.claim: Naml’s certain سآتيكم fits the absence of fear there and the honor shown Moses; Qasas’s hopeful لعلي آتيكم fits a frightened speaker unable to promise what will happen.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r4.anchor: وذلك أن مقام الخوف في القصص لم يدعه يقطع بالأمر فإن الخائف لا يستطيع القطع بما سيفعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p549/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p549/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p549/r3.claim: He introduces Musa’s story in Naml and Qasas as another broad narrative comparison, to be studied through its many similarities and differences.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p549/r3.anchor: ومثال آخر على التشابه والاختلاف في القرآن الكريم ما جاء في سورتي النمل والقصص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p71/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p71/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p71/r1.claim: Al-Qasas gives a long account of Moses from before his birth through Pharaoh's drowning, while al-Naml gives only a brief summary; their expressions follow those different narrative scopes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p71/r1.anchor: فالقصة في سورة القصص إذن مفصلة مطولة، وفي سورة النمل موجزة مجملة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r4.claim: Al-Naml repeats the verb آتيكم before its two alternatives, whereas al-Qasas uses it once before the alternatives.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r4.anchor: كرر فعل الإتيان في النمل، فقال: "سَآتيكُمْ مِنها بِخَبر أو آتيكُمْ بِشِهابٍ"

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p464/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p464/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p464/r2.claim: The section recounts God's granting Moses prophethood and sending him to Pharaoh and his people with nine miracles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p464/r2.anchor: In this section, that part of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p464/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p464/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p464/r3.claim: The Moses account reassures the Prophet that revelation is God's favor, just as God chose Moses, and shows opponents that prophethood is not strange or alien.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p464/r3.anchor: Firstly, God has sent divine revelations to him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r1.claim: Although the Moses account has been explained in earlier sūrahs, Islahi focuses here on its coherence with the present sūrah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r1.anchor: This account of Moses (sws) has been mentioned

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r2.claim: Prophethood is an uncommon, divinely selected task; those chosen for it need time to become accustomed to it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r2.anchor: Only those people experience it who the Almighty selects for this special task.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r3.claim: The audience, too, finds prophethood unfamiliar and raises doubts and objections when it is presented.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p465/r3.anchor: those before whom it was presented also regarded it to be something unique and strange

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r1.claim: Stories of earlier prophets console the Prophet through their experience and observations, while presenting opponents with conclusive truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r1.anchor: so that the Prophet (sws) could find assurance and comfort through their experiences and observations and his rivals were also conveyed the truth in a conclusive way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r2.claim: Moses most resembles Muhammad; his life is detailed in the Torah, and the Israelites who claimed faith in Moses opposed Muhammad, making this account suited to reassure the Prophet and instruct his rivals.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r2.anchor: The prophet and messenger who resembled Mu ḥammad (sws) the most

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r3.claim: Though the Prophet is addressed in the story, its direction of address is toward his rivals.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r3.anchor: the direction of address is towards his rivals.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r4.claim: Prophethood and messengerhood are God's gift, not something a person can obtain by his own effort, unlike learned crafts and professions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r4.anchor: It is evident from this verse that propehthood and messengerhood is a blessing and gift of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r5.claim: God trains and instructs prophets; they are not students of teachers or seminaries and do not seek appointment, but are prepared through trials and tests.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r5.anchor: God Himself trains and instructs a prophet and a messenger.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r6.claim: Joseph's training in an Egyptian jail and Moses' service tending Jethro's goats in Midian exemplify God's preparation of prophets through their lives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r6.anchor: Joseph (sws) was trained and instructed in a jail of Egypt.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r7.speaker: David (sws)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r7.claim: David is reported to have said that God took him from tending the flock and appointed him ruler over Israel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r7.anchor: David (sws) is reported to have said about himself

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r8.claim: Moses tended Jethro's goats in Midian and, lost on a dark cold night while returning, saw a light and went seeking directions or an ember to warm his family.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p466/r8.anchor: He lost his way on a dark and cold night

IBNMUJAHID:v1p487/r10.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p487/r10.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p487/r10.claim: Ibn Mujāhid counts 27 possessive yāʾs in the sūra, six disputed; the excerpt names the first four locations.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p487/r10.anchor: ياءات الإضافة فى هذه السورة سبع وعشرون ياء إضافة اختلفوا فى ست منهن ﴿ آنست نارا ﴾

NASHR:v2p337/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p337/r1.speaker: الكوفيون ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p337/r1.claim: The Kufans and Yaʿqūb read tanwīn on shihāb; the other readers do not, making the following word a construct complement.
NASHR:v2p337/r1.anchor: فقرأ الكوفيون ويعقوب بالتنوين، وقرأ الباقون بغير الرسم

NASHR:v2p340/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p340/r2.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p340/r2.claim: These readers open the first-person yāʾ in إني آنست نارا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r3.claim: Muhammad is told to recall Moses speaking to his family while traveling from Midian to Egypt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r3.anchor: {إذ قال موسى لأهله} أي: واذكر يا محمد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r4.claim: Ānastu nāran means I saw a fire.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r5.claim: Moses tells his family to stay while he brings news of the route, which he had lost.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r5.anchor: {سآتيكم منها بخبر} أي: امكثوا مكانكم، سآتيكم بخبر عن الطريق، وكان قد ترك الطريق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r6.speaker: أهل الكوفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r6.claim: The Kufans read shihābin with tanwīn, making qabas an adjective of shihāb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r6.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة: "بشهاب" بالتنوين، جعلوا القبس نعتا للشهاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r7.speaker: الباقون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r7.claim: Other readers omit tanwīn and use an annexation that joins two near-synonyms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r7.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بلا تنوين على الإضافة، وهو إضافة الشيء إلى نفسه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r8.claim: Qabas is a brand with fire at one end and no fire at the other.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r8.anchor: وهو العود الذي في أحد طرفيه نار، وليس في الطرف الآخر نار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r9.claim: Some say shihāb is a luminous column; Arabs call any white shining thing a shihāb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الشهاب هو شيء ذو نور، مثل العمود، والعرب تسمي كل أبيض ذي نور شهابا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r10.claim: Qabas can mean a piece of fire.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r11.claim: Taṣṭalūn means to warm yourselves from the cold; the scene occurred in severe winter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p144/r11.anchor: لعلكم تصطلون} تستدفئون من البرد، وكان ذلك في شدة الشتاء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r1.claim: The phrase expresses the hope that the people might warm themselves by the fire; ṣilāʾ means a great fire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:7-8/r1.anchor: رجاء أن تستدفئوا بها والصلاء النار العظيمة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r1.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r1.claim: Al-Baghawī reports that some define a flame as a column-like luminous thing, and Arabs call any white luminous object a flame; a qabas is a piece of fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r1.anchor: وقال البغوي : وقال بعضهم : الشهاب شيء ذو نور مثل العمود

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r2.claim: Kufian readers vocalize shihāban with nunation and construe qabas as apposition or description.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r2.anchor: فقراءة الكوفيين بالتنوين على البدل أو الوصف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r3.speaker: غيرهم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r3.claim: Other readers use a genitive construction because qabas is the more specific term.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r3.anchor: وقراءة غيرهم بالإضافة , لأن القبس أخص

BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p410/r4.claim: It was a cold night, so Moses hoped the fire would warm his family on his return.

DURR-FULL:v6p340/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p340/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p340/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas defines a flame-brand as a tongue of fire taken to kindle from, affirms Arab usage, and cites Tarafa's line comparing something to a brand.
DURR-FULL:v6p340/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله عز وجل {بشهاب قبس} قال: شعلة من نار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r1.speaker: الزجاج والزمخشري وغيرهما
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj, al-Zamakhshari, and others take إذ as an object governed by an omitted اذكر and as a general time expression, not a temporal adverb, paralleling 2:30.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r1.anchor: الزجاج والزمخشري وغيرهما : انتصب { إذ } بفعل مضمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r2.claim: The new passage parallels the Prophet's receiving the Quran with Moses receiving God's speech when called, It is a deft transition from praise of revelation to prophetic stories.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r2.anchor: ومناسبة موقعها إفادة تنظير تلقي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن بتلقي موسى عليه السلام كلام الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r3.claim: The story follows praise of the Quran as a transition to the next kind of Quranic inimitability: reporting unseen events, counted as the fourth aspect in the tenth introductory discussion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r3.anchor: وذلك من بديع التخلص إلى ذكر قصص هؤلاء الأنبياء عقب التنويه بالقرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r4.claim: The narrative that begins with Moses speaking to his family prepares for the call in 27:8; his remark came as he was about to receive revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r4.anchor: تمهيد لجملة { فلما جاءها نودي أن بورك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r5.claim: The story serves as a model for Muhammad and his people, embedding Moses's pre-mission circumstances in an admonition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r5.anchor: فهذه القصة مثل ضربه الله لحال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع قومه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r6.claim: Al-ahl means Moses's wife: she was the addressee, and he had only her and two young sons with him; al-ahl is a euphemistic way to refer to a wife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r6.anchor: مراد به زوجه ، ولم يكن معه إلا زوجه وابنان صغيران

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r7.speaker: الحديث
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r7.claim: Ibn Ashur cites the hadith wording والله ما علمت على أهلي إلا خيرا as usage of al-ahl for one's wife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r7.anchor: والله ما علمت على أهلي إلا خيرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r8.claim: The fire appeared only to Moses because it was an otherworldly light shown to him, not an ordinary fire; the emphatic إن suggests his wife doubted its appearance since she could not see it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p224/r8.anchor: ولم تظهر النار إلا لموسى دون غيره من أهله لأنها لم تكن نارا معتادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r1.claim: Al-inas is sensing or noticing something subtle, whether seen or heard; al-Harith ibn Hilliza's line is cited for the verb آنست.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r1.anchor: الإحساس والشعور بأمر خفي ، فيكون في المرئيات وفي الأصوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r2.claim: The requested khabar is news about the place from which the fire appears.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r2.anchor: والمراد بالخبر خبر المكان الذي تلوح منه النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r3.claim: Moses may have hoped to find a household that would host them, or travelers with an ember to light roadside wood and warm the family.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r3.anchor: ولعله ظن أن هنالك بيتا يرجو استضافتهم إياه وأهله تلك الليلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r4.claim: A shihab is a burning ember; a qabas is an ember or flame taken from another fire to kindle wood or a wick.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r4.anchor: الجمر المشتعل . والقبس : جمرة أو شعلة نار تقبس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r5.claim: The majority read شهاب قبس as an annexation of a general term to a specific one, like خاتم حديد.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r5.anchor: قرأ الجمهور بإضافة { شهاب } إلى { قبس } إضافة العام إلى الخاص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r6.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r6.claim: Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, Yaqoub, and Khalaf read شهاب with nunation; قبس is then either an appositive or an adjective.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r6.anchor: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب وخلف بتنوين { شهاب }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r7.claim: Iṣṭilāʾ is an iftiʿāl form from burning or roasting by fire; its form conveys trying to warm oneself by the fire's heat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p225/r7.anchor: افتعال من الصلي وهو الشي بالنار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r5.claim: The narrative shifts with an implied “remember when”; Moses was traveling with his wife, Shuʿayb's daughter, toward Egypt near the time of his prophethood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r5.anchor: ثم قص تعالى خبر موسى، والتقدير اذكر إذ قال موسى وكان من أمر موسى عليه السلام أنه حين خرج بزوجه بنت شعيب عليه السلام يريد مصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r6.claim: آنست means “I saw”; Ḥassān ibn Thābit's verse illustrates the usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r6.anchor: وآنست معناه رأيت، ومنه قول حسان بن ثابت: [المنسرح] انظر خليلي بباب جلق هل تؤنس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r7.claim: Moses and his wife were in a dark, cold, rainy night, had lost their fire and way, were chilled and in darkness, and his fire-sticks had failed when he saw fire at a distance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r7.anchor: في ليلة ظلماء ذات برد ومطر ففقدوا النار ومسهم البرد واشتدت عليهم الظلمة وضلوا الطريق وأصلد زناد موسى عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r10.claim: شهاب evokes a flame taken at the tip of a stick; قبس specifies fire obtained by kindling, unlike meteors that need not be kindled.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r10.anchor: وقوله بشهاب قبس شبه النار التي تؤخذ في طرف عود أو غيره ب «الشهاب»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r11.claim: القبس is a piece of fire taken onto a stick or other object, by analogy with قبض for something grasped.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p249/r11.anchor: و «القبس» اسم لقطعة النار تقتبس في عود أو غيره كما القبض اسم ما يقبض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the people of Kufa call the fire-stick المجهولة.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p250/r1.anchor: قال الطبري: ويسميها أهل الكوفة المجهولة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir frames the passage as a reminder of God choosing and speaking privately to Moses, giving him striking signs, and sending him to Pharaoh's elite, who rejected them arrogantly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r1.anchor: مذكرا له ما كان من أمر موسى، كيف اصطفاه الله وكلمه، وناجاه وأعطاه من الآيات العظيمة الباهرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r2.claim: Moses was traveling with his family, lost the way during a dark night, and saw a fire from the side of the Mount.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r2.anchor: أي: اذكر حين سار موسى بأهله، فأضل الطريق، وذلك في ليل وظلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r3.claim: The verb describes Moses seeing a blazing, flaring fire.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r4.claim: Moses hoped to learn the route or bring back a firebrand so his family could warm themselves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r4.anchor: أي: عن الطريق، {أو آتيكم بشهاب قبس لعلكم تصطلون} أي: تتدفؤون به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r5.claim: His prediction came true: he returned with momentous news and took from the fire a great light.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p179/r5.anchor: وكان كما قال، فإنه رجع منها بخبر عظيم، واقتبس منها نورا عظيما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r1.claim: Temporal إذ is governed by an omitted اذكر, introducing Moses' story as another sign of divine wisdom and knowledge; it may instead be governed by عليم.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r1.anchor: { إذ } منصوب بمضمر ، وهو : اذكر ، كأنه قال على أثر ذلك : خذ من آثار حكمته وعلمه قصة موسى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r2.claim: A report says Moses was accompanied only by his wife, whom God called his family; this explains the plural address.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r2.anchor: وروي أنه لم يكن مع موسى عليه السلام غير امرأته ، وقد كنى الله عنها بالأهل ، فتبع ذلك ورود الخطاب على لفظ الجمع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r3.claim: الشهاب is a flame; القبس is fire taken from another fire, and a flame can be a firebrand or not.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r3.anchor: الشهاب : الشعلة . والقبس : النار المقبوسة ، وأضاف الشهاب إلى القبس لأنه يكون قبسا وغير قبس .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r4.claim: With tanwīn on قبس, it can be read as an appositive or adjective because it carries the sense of firebrand.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتنوين : جعل القبس بدلا ، أو صفة لما فيه من معنى القبس .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r5.claim: خبر means information about the road, which Moses had lost.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r5.anchor: والخبر : ما يخبر به عن حال الطريق ، لأنه كان قد ضله .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r6.claim: The contrast between a confident promise and “perhaps” is no contradiction: strong hope can prompt a promise while allowing failure.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r6.anchor: قد يقول الراجي إذا قوي رجاؤه : سأفعل كذا ، وسيكون كذا مع تجويزه الخيبة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r7.claim: The future prefix سـ promises his family that he will bring news even if delayed, perhaps because the distance was long.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r7.anchor: فإن قلت : كيف جاء بسين التسويف ؟ قلت : عدة لأهله أنه يأتيهم به وإن أبطأ ، أو كانت المسافة بعيدة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r8.claim: أو expresses that if Moses failed to obtain both things, he expected at least guidance or fire, trusting God not to combine two deprivations.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r8.anchor: قلت بني الرجاء على أنه إن لم يظفر بحاجتيه جميعا لم يعدم واحدة منهما : إما هداية الطريق ؛ وإما اقتباس النار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r9.claim: Moses did not yet know he would receive both great outcomes: worldly honor and honor in the afterlife.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p354/r9.anchor: وما أدراه حين قال ذلك أنه ظافر على النار بحاجتيه الكليتين جميعا ، وهما العزان : عز الدنيا ، وعز الآخرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r1.claim: Abu ʿUbayda glosses ānastu as I saw a fire, explaining that people are called ins because they can be seen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما : رأيت نارا , قاله أبو عبيدة ومنه سمي الإنساء إنسا لأنهم مرئيون

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r2.claim: Qatada glosses ānastu as I sensed a fire; the word denotes perception from a familiar or reassuring direction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : أحسست نارا , قاله قتادة , والإيناس : الإحساس من جهة يؤنس بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r3.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r3.claim: Ibn Shajara interprets the promised report as knowledge about the fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما : سأخبركم عنها بعلم , قاله ابن شجرة . الثاني : بخبر الطريق

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the report is about the route, since Moses had lost his way.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r4.anchor: الثاني : بخبر الطريق , لأنه قد كان ضل الطريق , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r5.claim: A shihab is a luminous ray; a star whose light streaks across the sky is consequently called a shihab.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r5.anchor: والشهاب الشعاع المضي , ومنه قيل للكوكب الذي يمر ضوؤه في السماء شهاب

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r6.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r6.claim: The cited poet likens a spearhead to the flame of a firebrand, illustrating the imagery of a glowing flame.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر : في كفه صعدة مثقفة … فيها سنان كشعلة القبس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r7.claim: Qabas is a piece taken from a fire; borrowing knowledge is also called اقتباس because it illuminates like fire.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p193#2/r8.claim: Qatada says the phrase aims to warm the group from the cold and that it was winter.

MUQATIL:27:7-10/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r1.claim: Moses’s family member addressed here is his wife.
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r1.anchor: { إذ قال موسى لأهله } يعنى امرأته حين رأى النار

MUQATIL:27:7-10/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r2.claim: The fire Moses saw was the light of the Lord of Majesty, seen on Friday night to the mountain’s right in the Holy Land.
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r2.anchor: وهو نور رب العزة جل ثناؤه، رآه ليلة الجمعة

MUQATIL:27:7-10/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r3.claim: Moses had lost the road and hoped to learn the route; if no one could guide him, he would bring a bright torch so they could warm themselves.
MUQATIL:27:7-10/r3.anchor: أين الطريق، وقد كان تحير وترك الطريق

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r1.speaker: شاعر مجهول
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r1.claim: A quoted verse calls fire the fruit of winter and says those seeking winter fruit should warm themselves by it.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r1.anchor: النار فاكهة الشتاء فمن يرد أكل الفواكه شاتيا فليصطل

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says a shihāb is anything white and luminous.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r2.anchor: الزجاج: كل أبيض ذي نور فهو شهاب.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses shihāb simply as fire.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r4.speaker: أبو النجم
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r4.claim: Abū al-Najm’s poem depicts a shihāb burning brightly, then going out.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r4.anchor: قال أبو النجم: كأنما كان شهابا واقدا أضاء ضوءا ثم صار خامدا

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r5.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r5.claim: A shihāb originally means a stick with an ember at one end and no fire at the other.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r5.anchor: أحمد بن يحيى: أصل الشهاب عود في أحد طرفيه جمرة والآخر لا نار فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r6.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r6.claim: Al-Naḥḥās favors “a shining ray,” including a celestial body whose light extends across the sky; another poem compares a spearhead to a flame.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:8/r6.anchor: وقول النحاس فيه حسن: والشهاب الشعاع المضيء ومنه الكوكب الذي يمد ضوءه في السماء.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p634/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p634/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p634/r5.claim: A second sense is truthful or certain information, as in the hoopoe's report from Sheba.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p634/r5.anchor: والثاني : الصدق . ومنه قوله تعالى في النمل : ^ ( وجئتك من سباء بنبإ يقين ) ^
